E100.name: Curcumin
E100.reason: Natural yellow color derived from turmeric. Generally recognized as safe.

E101.name: Riboflavin (Vitamin B2)
E101.reason: A B vitamin used as yellow food coloring. Safe.

E102.name: Tartrazine
E102.reason: Synthetic yellow dye. Linked to hyperactivity in children and allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

E104.name: Quinoline Yellow
E104.reason: Synthetic dye. Banned in some countries. May cause hyperactivity.

E110.name: Sunset Yellow FCF
E110.reason: Synthetic orange-yellow dye. Linked to hyperactivity and allergic reactions.

E120.name: Cochineal / Carmine
E120.reason: Natural red dye from insects. Safe but not suitable for vegans.

E122.name: Azorubine / Carmoisine
E122.reason: Synthetic red dye. May cause allergic reactions and hyperactivity.

E124.name: Ponceau 4R
E124.reason: Synthetic red dye. Banned in US. Linked to hyperactivity.

E127.name: Erythrosine
E127.reason: Synthetic red dye. Linked to thyroid issues in high doses. Banned in several countries.

E129.name: Allura Red AC
E129.reason: Synthetic red dye. Linked to hyperactivity in children.

E131.name: Patent Blue V
E131.reason: Synthetic blue dye. May cause allergic reactions. Banned in some countries.

E132.name: Indigotine / Indigo Carmine
E132.reason: Synthetic blue dye. May cause nausea and hypertension in sensitive individuals.

E133.name: Brilliant Blue FCF
E133.reason: Synthetic blue dye. Generally considered safe by FDA and EFSA.

E141.name: Copper Complexes of Chlorophylls
E141.reason: Green colorant derived from chlorophyll. Safe.

E150a.name: Plain Caramel
E150a.reason: Simple caramel coloring from heated sugar. Safe.

E150d.name: Sulphite Ammonia Caramel
E150d.reason: Contains 4-MEI (4-methylimidazole), classified as possibly carcinogenic by IARC.

E160a.name: Beta-Carotene
E160a.reason: Natural orange pigment, precursor to Vitamin A. Safe.

E160b.name: Annatto
E160b.reason: Natural orange-red colorant from seeds. Generally safe.

E170.name: Calcium Carbonate
E170.reason: Natural mineral used as white coloring and calcium supplement. Safe.

E200.name: Sorbic Acid
E200.reason: Natural preservative. Generally recognized as safe.

E202.name: Potassium Sorbate
E202.reason: Common preservative. Safe at permitted levels.

E210.name: Benzoic Acid
E210.reason: Preservative. May form benzene when combined with Vitamin C (ascorbic acid).

E211.name: Sodium Benzoate
E211.reason: Preservative. Linked to hyperactivity in children when combined with certain dyes. May form benzene with Vitamin C.

E212.name: Potassium Benzoate
E212.reason: Similar concerns to sodium benzoate. May form benzene with ascorbic acid.

E220.name: Sulphur Dioxide
E220.reason: Preservative. Can trigger asthma attacks and allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

E223.name: Sodium Metabisulphite
E223.reason: Sulphite preservative. Dangerous for asthmatics and sulphite-sensitive people.

E249.name: Potassium Nitrite
E249.reason: Preservative in cured meats. Can form carcinogenic nitrosamines.

E250.name: Sodium Nitrite
E250.reason: Used in processed meats. WHO classifies processed meats with nitrites as Group 1 carcinogen.

E251.name: Sodium Nitrate
E251.reason: Converts to nitrite in body. Potential carcinogen risk with processed meats.

E270.name: Lactic Acid
E270.reason: Naturally occurring acid. Safe and widely used.

E300.name: Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C)
E300.reason: Essential vitamin used as antioxidant. Safe.

E319.name: TBHQ (Tert-Butylhydroquinone)
E319.reason: Synthetic antioxidant. High doses linked to nausea and vision issues. EFSA set strict ADI.

E320.name: BHA (Butylated Hydroxyanisole)
E320.reason: Synthetic antioxidant. IARC classifies as possibly carcinogenic to humans (Group 2B).

E321.name: BHT (Butylated Hydroxytoluene)
E321.reason: Synthetic antioxidant. Controversial â€” some studies link to cancer, others show safety.

E322.name: Lecithin
E322.reason: Natural emulsifier from soy or sunflower. Safe.

E330.name: Citric Acid
E330.reason: Naturally occurring in citrus fruits. Safe.

E338.name: Phosphoric Acid
E338.reason: Used in colas. High intake linked to bone density loss and kidney issues.

E339.name: Sodium Phosphates
E339.reason: Excess phosphate intake linked to cardiovascular and kidney issues.

E341.name: Calcium Phosphates
E341.reason: Raising agent and acidity regulator. Generally safe at food levels.

E407.name: Carrageenan
E407.reason: Thickener from seaweed. Some studies link to gut inflammation, though debated.

E412.name: Guar Gum
E412.reason: Natural thickener from guar beans. Safe at food-use levels.

E415.name: Xanthan Gum
E415.reason: Common thickener. Safe at food-use levels.

E420.name: Sorbitol
E420.reason: Sugar alcohol. Safe but excessive intake may cause digestive issues.

E422.name: Glycerol
E422.reason: Naturally occurring. Safe as food additive.

E433.name: Polysorbate 80
E433.reason: Synthetic emulsifier. Some animal studies link to gut inflammation. Under review by EFSA.

E450.name: Diphosphates
E450.reason: Phosphate additive. Excess linked to cardiovascular risk.

E451.name: Triphosphates
E451.reason: Phosphate additive. Same concerns as other phosphates.

E460.name: Cellulose
E460.reason: Plant fiber used as bulking agent. Safe.

E466.name: Carboxymethyl Cellulose
E466.reason: Synthetic thickener. Some studies suggest it may alter gut microbiome.

E471.name: Mono- and Diglycerides
E471.reason: Emulsifiers derived from fats. Generally safe.

E508.name: Potassium Chloride
E508.reason: Salt substitute. Safe at food-use levels.

E621.name: Monosodium Glutamate (MSG)
E621.reason: Flavour enhancer. May cause headaches, flushing in sensitive individuals (Chinese Restaurant Syndrome). FSSAI permits with limits.

E627.name: Disodium Guanylate
E627.reason: Flavour enhancer, often paired with MSG. Should be avoided by gout patients (purine source).

E631.name: Disodium Inosinate
E631.reason: Flavour enhancer. Avoid if prone to gout. Often used with MSG.

E635.name: Disodium 5'-Ribonucleotides
E635.reason: Combination of E627 and E631. Avoid with gout.

E900.name: Dimethylpolysiloxane
E900.reason: Anti-foaming agent (used in cooking oils at restaurants). Safe at food levels.

E950.name: Acesulfame Potassium
E950.reason: Artificial sweetener. Some studies raise concerns, but FDA/EFSA approve it. Ongoing research.

E951.name: Aspartame
E951.reason: Artificial sweetener. IARC classified as possibly carcinogenic (Group 2B) in 2023. EFSA maintains current ADI is safe.

E952.name: Cyclamate
E952.reason: Artificial sweetener. Banned in US since 1969. Still permitted in EU/India with limits.

E954.name: Saccharin
E954.reason: Oldest artificial sweetener. Previously linked to bladder cancer in rats, but delisted as carcinogen.

E955.name: Sucralose
E955.reason: Artificial sweetener. Generally safe, but some studies question long-term gut microbiome effects.

E960.name: Steviol Glycosides (Stevia)
E960.reason: Natural sweetener from stevia plant. Safe.

E965.name: Maltitol
E965.reason: Sugar alcohol. Safe but may cause digestive issues in excess.

E1442.name: Hydroxypropyl Distarch Phosphate
E1442.reason: Modified starch. Generally safe but indicates ultra-processing.

E1450.name: Starch Sodium Octenyl Succinate
E1450.reason: Modified starch. Safe but marker of ultra-processing.
